{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the lower tail (stroke 4) at the start and traced it from the crossing outward over several passes, standing dominoes back up where needed. That stroke is part of the fish silhouette the judge sees. The table's fish, with its body, both tails and nose, was lit and connected to the start for the push, and the lower tail is part of that outline.

Execution: I picked one stroke and stuck with it, working steadily without pulling others off their own pieces. I used several close inspections of the loop and crossing area to check what was connected and report it back accurately. When the crossing and loop were being worked on, I kept my hands off so nobody got bumped.

Collaboration: I stayed clear of the corner Hana and Sofia were working on, so we didn't knock each other's work over. I confirmed plans out loud, gave credit to Hana and Omar for the body and upper tail, and told the table what I could see from my inspections. I backed Sofia's and Hana's fixes rather than competing with them.

Leadership: I led by example on discipline. I committed to a stroke early, called out my status clearly, and joined the hands-off call before the push to protect the lit fish. I supported Hana's plan and kept the table's communication calm and positive in the last minutes.

Overall, I delivered my assigned piece of a fish that reads clearly as a fish, and I helped keep the table stable through the final stretch.", "my_share_percent": 22}
